solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Note down the highest score ever?

definitions.meaning: to note something down is to write it into a log or register
the best figure ever achieved, a sporting best that stands in the books

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they should jot down what looks like an all-time top score.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to write down or register; as a noun it is the best performance yet achieved.

clue.text: Intervening in desperate scrap, judge finally sums up

indicators.note: something intervening comes between, so this letter goes into the middle of the jumbled letters
desperate suggests wild disorder, so the letters of scrap are rearranged
finally points to the closing letter of the word judge

explanation.surface: In the middle of a frantic fight, a judge at last steps in and summarises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' turns SCRAP into RCAPS, and 'Intervening in' puts E, the last letter of judge from 'finally', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap is a summary, so the verb recaps means summarises, matching sums up.

clue.text: Grandfather maybe witnessing activity of bored employee?

parts.note: a grandfather clock is a tall pendulum clock, so a grandfather is an example of a timepiece
witnessing means watching

explanation.surface: A grandfather observing what a bored worker gets up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grandfather' looks like a relative; it is the tall longcase pendulum clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A bored worker keeps checking the time, waiting for the shift to end; that habit has this name.

clue.text: Regret overheard gibe, and waffle

indicators.note: overheard means the word is caught by ear, so we write letters that sound like it

parts.note: to regret is to rue
a gibe is a barb, a cutting remark

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry to have heard a taunt, and some empty talk.
explanation.walkthrough: RUE said aloud gives RHU, the first part of the plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense or meaningless chatter, the same idea as waffle.

clue.text: A peak volume

parts.note: a peak is a mountain, abbreviated mount

explanation.surface: A mountain-top, or perhaps a book: a terse phrase of nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Volume in the sense of quantity or quantity of something, a synonym.

clue.text: I wander uphill to see native New Zealander

indicators.note: in a down clue going uphill means reading the letters from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to wander is to roam

explanation.surface: A walker heads up a slope hoping to meet an indigenous New Zealander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uphill' turns I ROAM upside down in the down grid entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the Polynesian people indigenous to New Zealand.

clue.text: Latest out, umpteenth I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine or make elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The newest one is released, and the speaker supposes it is about the hundredth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' reads as 'I imagine' but tells you to rearrange OUT and UMPTEENTH I together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completely current or most recent is described with this phrase, a synonym for latest.

clue.text: Holding tureen is complicated

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled, so the letters of the word tureen are mixed up

explanation.surface: Carrying a soup dish turns out to be tricky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' looks like gripping the dish; it is the noun, possession or occupancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the holding of an office or property, so a holding in that sense.

clue.text: Credit quote convoluted: it involves going through hoops

parts.note: CR is the standard accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: convoluted means twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tangled reference about something requiring a lot of bureaucratic effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going through hoops' suggests jumping through hoops for officials; here the hoops are literal.
explanation.definitionFit: This lawn game is played by striking balls with mallets through small wire arches called hoops.

clue.text: Outstanding spinner has trophy, perhaps, to lift

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins

indicators.note: in a down clue to lift means to raise the word so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a trophy is an example of a reward

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler wins a trophy and hoists it above the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a spin bowler in cricket; it is the toy that spins. 'to lift' turns REWARD upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for first-rate or of the highest class, hence outstanding.

clue.text: Figure seen on middle of sofa regularly

indicators.note: on means placed after, so this number follows the other piece
the middle of a word means its central letters, here those of sofa

parts.note: a figure is a number, such as ten

explanation.surface: A number is spotted sitting in the middle of a settee time after time.
explanation.definitionFit: Often and regularly both mean frequently, happening many times.

clue.text: A couple of kings happy to retire for real

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, so two kings are KK
being up means being cheerful or happy

explanation.surface: Two monarchs are genuinely pleased to step down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retire' reverses A, KK and UP together.
explanation.definitionFit: Pukka is an Anglo-Indian word meaning genuine or authentic, as in the slang 'for real'.

clue.text: Dog lead

definitions.meaning: a breed of gun dog that stands still aiming its muzzle at game
a lead here is a hint or tip that directs someone

explanation.surface: Dog lead: a leash for a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a breed of hunting dog, and also a clue or tip that points the way.

clue.text: Vegetable gold, black and green, I gathered

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: gathered means drawn together into folds, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vegetable described by its colours, gold, black and green, collected by the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' rearranges GREEN and I into ERGINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine, or eggplant, is a purple-skinned fruit used as a vegetable in cooking.

clue.text: Small animals in nonconformist groups

parts.note: sects are dissenting religious groups that break from the mainstream

explanation.surface: Creatures found among bands of dissenters.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects are tiny creatures, so they are an example of small animals.

clue.text: Mistake students raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters go upwards, reading from the bottom

parts.note: pupils are students

explanation.surface: An error that learners brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a minor error, a synonym for mistake.

clue.text: Gaol's opening: despicable type is free!

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here that of Gaol's

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible, treacherous person

explanation.surface: A villain escapes jail and is suddenly at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like released from prison; it means costing nothing. Gaol is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means without charge, so free in the sense of costing nothing.

clue.text: Poor Jack is in depressed condition

indicators.note: is in means this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to feel depressed is to feel low

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters of Jack are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unfortunate Jack is feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressed condition' looks like the definition; only 'condition' defines, and 'depressed' gives the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw, or tetanus, is a medical condition causing spasm of the jaw muscles.

clue.text: Massive job mujaheddin must keep up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
to keep is to hold inside, so the letters sit concealed within these words

explanation.surface: An enormous task that the fighters have to sustain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must keep' picks OBMUJ from 'job mujaheddin', and 'up' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo means very large, as in a jumbo jet, hence massive.

clue.text: Risk sliding around close to crevasse, for one going down mountain

indicators.note: around means placed so as to surround the other piece
sliding suggests letters slipping about, so the word Risk is rearranged
the close of a word is its last letter, here that of crevasse

explanation.surface: A dangerous slip near a deep crack in a glacier, a mountaineering hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliding' turns RISK into SKIR, and 'around' wraps it round E, the final letter of crevasse from 'close to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier descends slopes on skis, so is someone travelling down a mountain.

clue.text: Square, primarily, in proper solid shape

indicators.note: in means this letter is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper or prudish

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, pointing to the opening letter of Square

explanation.surface: A square-looking item, mainly fitted in the right sort of solid figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like the shape; only its first letter, S, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A prism is a three-dimensional geometric figure with two identical parallel ends.

clue.text: Report result of tight vote?

definitions.meaning: to report is to relate or tell a story
a very close election often leads to the ballots being tallied a second time

explanation.surface: A news report on what happens after a knife-edge election.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount is to narrate, while a recount is a second counting of votes after a narrow outcome.

clue.text: Unlikely flier, one strange bird!

parts.note: from the saying 'pigs might fly', meaning something will never happen

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters of one are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a peculiar bird that hardly seems able to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigeon is a common bird, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Evaluate female equine?

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, a member of the horse family
-ess is the suffix that makes a female form, as in lioness

explanation.surface: A query whether this is a she-donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the answer as a feminine form of donkey, like lioness.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to judge the value or quality of something, a synonym for evaluate.
